::: {#fig-logistic-function}

```{r}
#| label: logistic-function-plot
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   The logistic function over z from -6 to 6, an S-shaped curve
#|   rising from near 0 on the left to near 1 on the right.
#|   Dotted horizontal lines mark the values 0 and 1, which the curve approaches but never reaches.
#|   Three points are marked, at z = -2, 0 and 2,
#|   with the middle one at height 0.5.
z_grid <- seq(-6, 6, length.out = 241)
logistic_curve <- data.frame(z = z_grid, sigmoid = plogis(z_grid))
logistic_points <- data.frame(z = c(-2, 0, 2), sigmoid = plogis(c(-2, 0, 2)))
logistic_points$label <- sprintf("%.3f", logistic_points$sigmoid)

logistic_function_plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(
    yintercept = c(0, 1),
    linetype = "dotted",
    colour = "grey50"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(
    data = logistic_curve,
    ggplot2::aes(x = z, y = sigmoid),
    colour = "#0072B2"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = logistic_points,
    ggplot2::aes(x = z, y = sigmoid, text = label),
    size = 3,
    colour = "#D55E00"
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(
    data = logistic_points,
    ggplot2::aes(x = z, y = sigmoid, label = label),
    nudge_x = 0.2,
    nudge_y = -0.06,
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-6, 6, 2)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "z", y = "logistic(z)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  plotly::ggplotly(logistic_function_plot, tooltip = "text")
} else {
  logistic_function_plot
}
```

The [logistic function](#def-logistic-function).
Its [values](#def-value) lie strictly between $0$ and $1$, and the marked points are the values at $z = -2$, $0$ and $2$ from @exm-logistic-function.

:::
